key_insight: A tailored U(1) quantum link model mapped to qubits can capture real-time string dynamics on digital quantum hardware, matching reference theory at short times and thermal behavior at long times.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that hardware-aware lattice design and error mitigation can make near-term quantum computers useful for studying confining gauge dynamics that are difficult for classical Monte Carlo methods.
method: Encode the gauge theory using dual height variables on qubits
Choose a lattice geometry matched to IBM heavy-hex connectivity to reduce non-adjacent couplings
Run quantum quenches from an initial string state and compare dynamics to tensor-network references
evidence_signal: Experiments on IBM hardware with up to 112 qubits showed good agreement with tensor-network calculations at short times and with thermal averages at long times, including near the phase transition.
watch_item: Noise still causes local gauge-symmetry violations, so accuracy depends on error mitigation and the chosen lattice/hardware match.
paper_title: String dynamics of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model on a digital quantum computer
